title: Introduce control-plane secondary subnet prober and PrivateLink consistency checker
author: Maya Saldana
description: Motivation: customers operating private control planes across multiple AZs sometimes need safe, automated validation of candidate secondary subnets during scale, upgrade, or failover workflows. Misconfigured route tables, NACLs, or security groups and mismatched PrivateLink endpoint DNS/service mappings are frequent causes of control-plane connectivity incidents. This PR implements a conservative, opt-in prober and reconciliation flow that validates a secondary subnet before it is used for control-plane traffic and performs non-destructive remediation for a small class of predictable issues. High-level changes: 1) new subnet prober binary (installer/pkg/prober) that runs as a short-lived sidecar in the control-plane agent DaemonSet; it performs idempotent checks: route table reachability to control-plane egress proxies, presence of required SG rules, NACL permissiveness for control-plane ports, and validation of PrivateLink endpoint DNS names and service-owner mappings. 2) SG reconciler (installer/pkg/reconciler) that can add missing, minimal allow rules for the control-plane agent -> endpoint flows when an autoscale/upgrade path is blocked and the cluster is in a safe, operator-approved state. Reconciler only adds rules matching a restricted template and records the change in provisioner audit logs for manual review. 3) Terraform updates: modules now export a data source for candidate-subnet metadata and create a lightweight IAM role for the prober so it can query EC2/TGW/Route53 APIs in cross-account installs. 4) Helm changes: a new values.toggle (controlPlane.prober.enabled) and templates to inject the prober container; the control-plane agent image includes the prober binary. 5) Installer CLI and Helm migration docs with explicit rollout steps and a safe rollback path that drains new subnets if prober checks fail during canary. Testing and rollout: added e2e tests that simulate a misconfigured subnet (missing SG rule and stale PrivateLink service name) and validate that the prober detects the issues and that the reconciler can fix the SG rule while leaving DNS mismatches for operator review. CI initially failed due to an intermittent race in the prober's Route53 query; fixed by adding exponential backoff and tighter timeouts. Rollout plan: opt-in via Helm value; recommend staged rollout (canary AZ) with prober.enabled=true and monitoring for audit log entries and prober metrics before enabling cluster-wide. Migration notes: terraform apply required to create the prober IAM role and grant read-only Route53 permissions; Helm addition is backward-compatible if prober.enabled=false. Security considerations: reconciler adds only narrowly-scoped SG entries and writes an immutable audit event; operators can set reconciler.mode=report-only to avoid auto-fixes. Impact: reduces manual interventions during subnet handoffs, prevents a class of control-plane outages, and adds observable audit trails for any automatic remediation.
commit_summary: Seven commits: add subnet prober implementation and unit tests; introduce SG reconciler and audit logging; Terraform data source + IAM role; Helm templates + values; e2e tests for prober flows; docs and migration guide; fix Route53 backoff race. Commits are small and focused to aid backporting.

ci_details: Pipeline: lint -> unit -> integration -> e2e. Lint: pass after IAM narrowing. Unit: pass. Integration: pass. E2E: initial run failed (Route53 race), subsequent run pass. Total runtime ~28m.
release_notes: Add optional control-plane subnet prober and PrivateLink consistency checker. Opt-in via Helm (controlPlane.prober.enabled). Adds a reconciler with report-only and auto-apply modes (reconciler.mode). Terraform requires creating a prober IAM role (see docs). Backwards-compatible when disabled. Recommended staged rollout. See docs/private_deployments/secondary-subnet-prober.md for full migration steps.
notes_for_rollback: If prober detects failures during canary, installer will mark new subnets as quarantined and the Helm post-install hook will abort adding them to the control-plane route table. To roll back: set controlPlane.prober.enabled=false and run helm rollback; terraform destroy is not required unless IAM role must be revoked. Reconciler auto-applied SG changes are recorded; operator runbook provides exact revert commands.
